location: Harrison Street near Columbia Square Street
narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomous mode was traveling in lane 4 on southwest-bound Harrison Street near Columbia Square in San Francisco. At that time a passenger car (Vehicle 2), traveling in the same direction ahead of the Zoox vehicle in the right adjacent lane (lane 5), was attempting to go around a cyclist, on the right side, in lane 5. The Zoox vehicle operator disengaged, Vehicle 2 then swerved left into lane 4 across the path of the Zoox vehicle and the driver-side quarter panel on Vehicle 2 contacted the passenger-side fender and front door of the Zoox vehicle. Both vehicles proceeded a few feet further and pulled over to exchange information. Vehicle 2 appeared to sustain minor damage and the Zoox vehicle did not sustain any damage. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

location: Frederick Street and Buena Vista Avenue
narrative: A Zoox vehicle operating in manual mode was eastbound on Frederick Street and turning right onto Buena Vista Avenue in San Francisco when the front wheel on the driver's side struck a traffic island to the left side of the vehicle. The wheel rim was damaged as a result of the interaction. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

location: Logue Avenue at E. Middlefield Road
narrative: On February 14, 2025 at 4:01 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in Mountain View, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Logue Avenue at E. Middlefield Road. The Waymo AV was traveling south on Logue Avenue and came to a stop at a red light in the dedicated right turn lane at the intersection with E. Middlefield Road. The Waymo AV proceeded from the stop line, and then came to a stop again before entering the E. Middlefield Road. A passenger car that was making a right turn directly behind the Waymo AV continued forward and the front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The passenger car sustained damage. Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 2 of Standing General Order 2021-01. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

manufacturer: MERCEDES-BENZ RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT NORTH AMERICA, INC.
location: BACK PARKING LOT OF NVIDIA ENDEAVOR
narrative: The subject Mercedes-Benz vehicle was driving in the back parking lot of the Nvidia Endeavor office complex in Santa Clara, CA (parallel to the San Tomas Aquino Creek). The Mercedes-Benz vehicle was driven in conventional mode to a stop adjacent to vehicles parked in the parking lot, and perpendicular to a parked Chevrolet Camaro. The driver in the Mercedes-Benz vehicle then shifted into Park (“P”) via the gearshift lever. While the Mercedes-Benz vehicle was stopped, the Chevrolet Camaro reversed out of its parking space and contacted the Mercedes-Benz vehicle at the right rear door. As a result, the right rear corner of the Chevrolet Camaro and the right rear passenger door of the Mercedes-Benz vehicle sustained minor damage. There were no reported injuries to any of the occupants. The incident is being reported under OL316 in an abundance of caution.

2021 Honda Accord CA 2 On Feb 5, 2025 at 06:31 PM PT, the blind spot sensor pod of our autonomous vehicle (AV) made contact with a parked passenger car on 2132 Kingsbury Cir, Santa Clara, CA. The AV was making a right turn along the Kingsbury Cir, traveling at 16 mph. Due to an inaccurate map version downloaded on the AV causing the AV to drive close to the parked vehicles on the side of the street, the safety driver disengaged the AV. After disengagement, the right side sensor pod of the AV made contact with the left side rear view mirror of a passenger vehicle parked on the side of the Kingsbury Cir. At the time of the impact, the AV's Level 4 ADS was not engaged and the safety driver was operating the AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained minor damage. Print Clear Form

narrative: On February 3, 2025 at 1:32 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Brisbane, California was in a collision involving a hand truck dolly on Bayshore Boulevard near Valley Drive. The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Bayshore Boulevard in the leftmost lane of two southbound lanes when an oncoming vehicle in the northbound lane struck a hand truck dolly, which was then projected from the northbound lane through the median lane and into the southbound lane occupied by the Waymo AV. The front of the Waymo AV then made contact with the hand truck dolly, which became lodged at the front of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV and the hand truck dolly sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was double parked, waiting for the next ride with brake lights and hazard lights activated, on southwest-bound Treat Avenue near Bryant Street in San Francisco. At that time, a passenger car (Vehicle 2) which had been parallel parked in the adjacent right curb lane, pulled out of the parking spot and began attempting a multi-point U-turn ahead of the Zoox vehicle. During the maneuver, Vehicle 2's driver's side rear door made contact with the front left fender of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the fender. The driver of Vehicle 2 pulled over after the collision to inspect both vehicles, then left the scene shortly after without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries and police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in manual mode was traveling northeast on Folsom Street and preparing to turn left onto 6th Street in San Francisco. At that time, a passenger car (Vehicle 2), traveling southeast on 6th Street, failed to stop for the red traffic light and entered the intersection, approaching the Zoox vehicle attempting a left turn. The front driver’s side of the passenger car collided with the driver-side rear wheel area of the Zoox vehicle. The front of the passenger car sustained damage however, the driver left the scene without exchanging information. The Zoox vehicle sustained moderate damage to the driver’s side rear wheel, and suspension, and was towed from the scene. The police were called to the scene and there were no reported injuries.

On January 23, 2025 at 5:09 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Jones Street near Union Street. The Waymo AV was stopped at the curb facing southbound on Jones Street. The Waymo AV then began reversing, and simultaneously a passenger car parked in a parking spot on Jones street to the left side of the Waymo AV began reversing from a parking spot. While both vehicles were backing, the rear driver side of the Waymo AV made contact with the rear passenger side of the passenger car. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

av_damage_areas: left rear passenger; front driver side
narrative: A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in autonomous mode, was traveling northeast on 11th Street approaching Folsom Street in San Francisco. A passenger car (Vehicle 2) was parallel parked on the right side of the roadway in the same direction as the Zoox vehicle. The passenger car pulled out of the parking spot and made a U-turn into the opposite travel lane, and unexpectedly crossed the double-yellow centerline and veered into the Zoox vehicle's travel lane. The Zoox vehicle braked in response to the encroaching passenger car however the passenger car made contact with the Zoox vehicle's driver's side fender and front and rear doors. The Zoox vehicle operator disengaged from autonomy and braked to a stop shortly after. The Zoox vehicle sustained major damage and had to be towed from the scene. The frontal airbags deployed on the passenger car and it sustained moderate damage to the front driver's side. The passenger car driver fled the scene and did not exchange information. The police were called to the scene and there were no reported injuries.

narrative: On January 21, 2025 at 5:57 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Fillmore Street near Bush Street. The Waymo AV was parked at the curb on northbound Fillmore Street when a passenger car in front of the Waymo AV pulled forward and then began to reverse in an attempt to leave its parking spot. As the passenger car continued to reverse, the rear driver side of the passenger car made contact with the front of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in autonomous mode, was stopped for a red traffic light on northbound Bryant Street at the intersection with 16th Street in San Francisco. A passenger car (Vehicle 2) was also stopped for the same traffic light directly behind the Zoox vehicle. After a few seconds, the passenger car started to inch forward and rear-ended the stopped Zoox vehicle, and the Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the rear bumper. There were no reported injuries at that time and the police were not called. The Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the passenger car driver was not looking ahead at the roadway before or at the time of contact. Zoox is submitting this updated report to include new information on notice of an unspecified injury allegation received on February 4, 2025, from the Zoox vehicle operator.

av_damage_areas: left rear; rear bumper; right rear
narrative: On January 15, 2025 at 1:12 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Stockton Street at Market Street. The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Stockton Street, approaching the five-way series of intersections with Ellis Street, Market Street, and 4th Street in order to proceed on 4th Street. The Waymo AV proceeded straight past the intersection where Ellis Street intersects Stockton Street, with an SUV following behind. Then, the traffic light turned red before the Waymo AV began to cross Market Street. The Waymo AV began slowing to stop within the crosswalk along Market Street, and the front of the trailing SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

2012 Subaru Forester 2 While traveling northbound on Pine Street in Martinez, a black vehicle pulled out of a driveway facing the road at the last second and collided with the passenger broad side of May's vehicle. May's vehicle is traveling at approximately 20 MPH in a residential neighborhood when this black vehicle exits a driveway facing the road and May's vehicle. This vehicle did not slow down or stop until entering into the roadway and collided with May's vehicle. May's vehicle operator attempts to swerve to the left but is unable to avoid a collision.

location: Parking garage at Mission Street and Angelo's Alley
narrative: On January 11, 2025 at 10:31 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car in a parking garage at Mission Street and Angelo’s Alley. The Waymo AV was traveling in a parking garage off of Mission Street and approached a passenger car that was stopped, facing the wrong direction in the opposing lane of travel. The Waymo AV began to proceed straight, passing the passenger car, when the passenger car began to reverse, maneuvering into the Waymo AV’s lane of travel, and the front passenger side of the passenger car made contact with the driver side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The passenger car sustained damage.

On January 11, 2025 at 4:41 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Venice Boulevard near National Boulevard. The Waymo AV was traveling northeast bound on Venice Boulevard in the middle of three lanes when a passenger car in the rightmost lane and in front of the Waymo AV began to change lanes to the middle lane. The test driver of the Waymo AV transitioned to manual mode, and began to change lanes into the leftmost lane to avoid the passenger car ahead. During this lane change maneuver, the rear driver side of the Waymo AV made contact with the front passenger side of an SUV that was traveling in the leftmost lane, positioned slightly behind the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The SUV sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1), operating in manual mode, was traveling north on Florida Street approaching Treat Avenue in San Francisco. The Zoox vehicle slowed to a stop to allow an oncoming tow truck (Vehicle 2) to clear. As the tow truck was passing the Zoox vehicle the driver's side mirror of the tow truck made contact with the roof-mounted sensor pod on the rear driver's side of the Zoox vehicle. The sensor pod on the Zoox vehicle sustained moderate damage. The tow truck operator left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

location: Angus Street near Lakewood Avenue N.

At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present in the driver’s seating position. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in manual mode was traveling westbound on 14th Street towards Folsom Street in San Francisco. The Zoox vehicle encountered a double-parked vehicle in the lane and went around it. After passing the double-parked vehicle, and as the Zoox vehicle was re-entering its travel lane, another parallel-parked passenger car (Vehicle 2) pulled out from a parking space ahead and entered the Zoox vehicle's travel path. The front bumper of the Zoox vehicle on the passenger side made contact with the driver's side fender of the passenger car. There were no reported injuries and the police were not called.

On December 27, 2024 at 10:16 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Larkin Street at Olive Street. The Waymo AV was traveling northbound on Larkin Street when a passenger car traveling directly in front of the Waymo AV stopped in lane, and began to reverse to parallel park at the curb. While the passenger car was reversing, the rear driver side of the passenger car made contact with the front passenger side of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

On December 25, 2024 at 8:40 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Broadway near Buchanan Street. The Waymo AV was parked at the curb in the westbound direction of Broadway street, in front of a parked passenger car, when another passenger car parallel parked in front of the Waymo AV within close proximity to the front of the Waymo AV. Due to the proximity of the now parked passenger car in front of the Waymo AV, the Waymo AV was unable to unpark from the curb, and the ADS was disengaged to maneuver the Waymo AV away from the curb. The Waymo AV was maneuvered in manual mode to unpark from the curb. During this maneuver, the test driver reversed the Waymo AV and the rear of the Waymo AV made contact with the front of the passenger car that was parked behind the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in conventional mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On December 20, 2024 at 3:55 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a fixed object (solar panel) in a parking lot at 8985 Venice Boulevard. The Waymo AV was traveling through a parking lot at a low rate of speed when the front driver side of the Waymo AV made contact with the corner of a solar panel situated to the left of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) operating in manual mode was in stop-and-go traffic in the left through lane on northbound Potrero Avenue at 24th Street in San Francisco. As the passenger car passed the Zoox vehicle, the passenger-side mirror of the passenger car swiped the radar unit on the driver-side quarter panel of the Zoox vehicle. There was minor damage to the Zoox vehicle. The driver of the passenger car did not stop and left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries and police were not called.

location: Van Ness Avenue at O'Farrell Street
narrative: On December 17, 2024 at 1:08 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Van Ness Avenue at O'Farrell Street. The Waymo AV was in autonomous mode traveling north in the rightmost of two lanes on Van Ness Avenue when it partially entered the left adjacent lane to make room for a cyclist on its right who was traveling in the same direction. A heavy truck behind in the left adjacent lane proceeded forward, and the Waymo AV test driver transitioned to manual mode immediately before the rear driver side of the Waymo AV made contact with the front passenger side of the heavy truck. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On December 16, 2024 at 1:58 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Toland Street at Jerrold Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling northeast on Toland Street. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection with Jerrold Avenue, a heavy truck initiated a wide left turn from southwest Toland Street onto southeast Jerrold Avenue. The Waymo AV came to a stop at the four-way stop sign to prepare to cross the intersection with Jerrold Avenue. While the heavy truck was partially on Toland Street and partially on Jerrold Avenue, the Waymo AV entered the intersection to maneuver around the right side of the heavy truck, but immediately came to a stop as the heavy truck began reversing. The passenger side of the heavy truck then made contact with the passenger side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

location: Alabama Street at Cesar Chavez Street
narrative: On December 14, 2024 at 9:53 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck on Alabama Street at Cesar Chavez Street. The Waymo AV was stopped facing a malfunctioning traffic light on southbound Alabama Street at the intersection with Cesar Chavez Street. While the Waymo AV remained stopped and the traffic light was not illuminated, a heavy truck that had been stopped behind the Waymo AV entered the oncoming lane of Alabama Street to maneuver around the Waymo AV. As the heavy truck was passing the stopped Waymo AV, the passenger side of the heavy truck made contact with the rear driver side corner of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On December 12, 2024, a Pony.ai AV test vehicle was involved in a minor incident while parked behind Pony.ai’s office at 3501 Gateway Boulevard in Fremont. A passenger vehicle, unaffiliated with the company, backed into the rear of the Pony.ai AV test vehicle while it was parked. The damage to both vehicles was cosmetic in nature. There were no injuries reported, and the police were not called.

On December 11, 2024 at 12:56 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a vacuum cleaner on Bayshore Boulevard at Silver Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Bayshore Boulevard in the left lane of two lanes when it encountered a vacuum cleaner laying on its side in the roadway within its lane and across the lane line separating the two lanes. The Waymo AV applied braking and the front passenger side tire of the Waymo AV made contact with the vacuum cleaner. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The vacuum cleaner sustained damage. Waymo is reporting this crash under Request No. 2 of Standing General Order 2021-01. Waymo may supplement or correct its reporting with additional information as it may become available.

A Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) in autonomy was stopped at a red light behind an SUV (Vehicle 2) in the right travel lane on southbound 11th Street at the intersection with Bryant and Division Streets in San Francisco. After the light turned green, the SUV proceeded straight, in the right lane, toward southbound Bryant Street. The Zoox vehicle also proceeded and transitioned into the left lane (also a through lane). While almost through the intersection, the SUV suddenly veered left across the path of the Zoox vehicle toward Division Street. The Zoox vehicle braked hard in response to the turning SUV and had almost reached a stop when the rear driver side of the SUV made contact with the passenger side front fender of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle then came to a full stop. The driver of the SUV left the scene without exchanging information. The Zoox vehicle cleared the intersection, proceeded down Bryant Street, briefly stopped again, and then pulled over on Bryant Street. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the passenger side front fender. The police were not called.

location: West Olympic Boulevard at South Sherbourne Drive

narrative: On December 2, 2024 at 7:58 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on West Olympic Boulevard at South Sherbourne Drive. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound on West Olympic Boulevard and slowing to a stop for a queue of traffic. A passenger car approached the Waymo AV from behind, and the front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

location: East 3rd Street at South Central Avenue
narrative: On December 2, 2024 at 10:54 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a plastic crate on East 3rd Street at South Central Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound in the center lane on East 3rd Street, crossing the intersection with South Central Avenue when the front passenger side of the Waymo AV made contact with a plastic crate that was in the roadway within the Waymo AV’s lane of travel. The contact with the Waymo AV caused the crate to move into the adjacent right lane, which was occupied by a scooterist. The front tire of the scooter made contact with the crate and the scooter and scooterist fell. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Given the speed at which the scooter was traveling at the time of the contact, the scooter may have sustained damage.

On November 30, 2024 at 12:44 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Kearny Street at Broadway. The Waymo AV was traveling northbound on Kearny Street and came to a stop behind an SUV that was stopped within the lane of travel. The SUV then began reversing and the Waymo AV also reversed until it came to a stop in front of a passenger vehicle behind it. The SUV continued to reverse and the rear of the SUV made contact with the front of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On November 27, 2024 at 6:21 PM PT, a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California, was in a collision involving a passenger car on Barneveld Avenue at Jerrold Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Barneveld Avenue and came to a stop at the 3-way stop sign controlled intersection of Jerrold Avenue, when a passenger car approached the Waymo AV from behind. The front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

location: In Intersection Coleman Ave Left turn to W Hedding St
narrative: On November 27th at 1:27pm, Car 1 (weride av) - while in autonomous mode - was making a legal, protected, left turn from Coleman Ave. Car 1, turning onto W Hedding St., performed the turn from the second lane from the left and was travelling 11 mph when Car 1 then slowed down while still in the intersection. It is at this time Car 1's safety driver disengaged Car 1 from autonomous mode by using the throttle; this put car 1 into manual mode. It is at this time when car 2 (Ford f-150 XLT), traveling at 18 mph and also making a left turn from Coleman Ave within the same lane as car 1, struck and rear ended car 1 while both cars were still in the intersection. Car 1 sustained minor damage to its rear bumper and car 2 sustained minor damage to front bumper. Both parties pulled over to exchange information. Car 2 did not provide Registration and Insurance for their respective car. Car 2's driver did give us driver's license information but the driver of the vehicle (car 2) at the time of the incident was a different person than that represented on the driver's license presented.

On November 26, 2024 at 5:57 PM PT, a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California, was involved in a collision involving a passenger car at the intersection of Venice Boulevard and Vermont Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling west on Venice Blvd, and approaching Vermont Ave in the leftmost of two through lanes proceeding straight. As the Waymo AV began to enter the intersection after the traffic light turned yellow, an eastbound passenger car, waiting to make a left turn onto northbound Vermont Ave, proceeded to initiate a left turn during the yellow traffic signal, and impacted the Waymo AV on the front driver side. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage and required towing services; the passenger in the passenger car reported a minor injury.

On November 26, 2024 at 3:48 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Culver City, California was in a collision involving a van at a shopping center located near 3816 Sepulveda Boulevard. The Waymo AV was exiting a shopping center driveway and yielding to traffic as it prepared to make a right onto northwestbound Sepulveda Boulevard when a van traveling directly behind the Waymo AV passed the Waymo AV on the left and proceeded to make a right turn onto northwestbound Sepulveda Boulevard. While passing the stopped Waymo AV, the van’s passenger side made contact with the rear driver side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On November 8, 2024 at 8:39 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a food truck on 26th Street near Valencia Street. The Waymo AV was traveling west on 26th Street when it came to a stop to yield to an oncoming food truck in a narrow roadway with parked vehicles on both sides of the street. As the food truck was passing the stopped Waymo AV, the front driver’s side of the food truck made contact with the front driver’s side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On November 5, 2024 at 08:56 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a shipping container that was being hauled by a pickup truck on Murray Street at Genebern Way. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Genebern Way in autonomous mode when it came to a stop at a stop sign to prepare to make a left turn onto westbound Murray Street. Immediately after, a pickup truck (hauling a gooseneck trailer carrying a shipping container) that had been traveling east on Murray Street came to a stop at a stop sign at the intersection with Genebern Way. While the pickup truck remained stopped, the Waymo AV proceeded through the intersection. As the Waymo AV was making a left turn through the intersection, the pickup truck entered the intersection to make a right turn onto southbound Genebern Way. After the Waymo AV partially entered westbound Murray Street, it came to a stop to yield to the pickup truck. The Waymo AV test driver then transitioned to manual mode. A moment later, while the Waymo AV remained stopped, the rear left corner of the shipping container made contact with the front driver side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On November 4, 2024 at 6:28 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Culver City, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Culver Boulevard near Sepulveda Boulevard. The Waymo AV was stopped in traffic for a red light on southwestbound Culver Boulevard with an SUV stopped directly behind the Waymo AV. Moments later, a passenger car traveling at a high rate of speed approached the stopped SUV from behind and made contact with the rear of the SUV. The front of the SUV then made contact with the rear of the stopped Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. All three vehicles sustained damage.

location: Cesar Chavez Street at Guerrero Street
narrative: On November 3, 2024 at 1:18 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving an ambulance on Cesar Chavez Street at Guerrero Street. The Waymo AV was traveling east in the leftmost of two lanes on Cesar Chavez Street. While the traffic light was yellow, the Waymo AV began to cross the intersection with Guerrero Street. As the Waymo AV was crossing the intersection, an ambulance traveling north on Guerrero Street (without lights and sirens activated) began to make a right turn onto eastbound Cesar Chavez Street. While the ambulance completed its right turn it crossed into the lane the Waymo AV was travling in and the front driver side of the ambulance then made contact with the rear passenger side door of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Wamo AV sustained damage.

location: Parking lot at 3775 Mountain View Avenue
narrative: On November 3, 2024 at 8:22 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck (tow truck) in a parking lot at 3775 Mountain View Avenue. The Waymo AV was parked in a stall of a parking lot at 3775 Mountain View Avenue when a tow truck traveling through the parking lot made contact with the rear passenger side of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

A Zoox vehicle in autonomous mode was stopped for a red traffic light on northbound Howard Street while preparing to turn left onto westbound 12th Street in San Francisco. After the light turned green the Zoox vehicle began to move forward and then slowed gradually to yield to a pedestrian with right of way in the crosswalk on 12th Street. Just as the Zoox vehicle slowed to almost a stop (0.2 mph), a skateboarder quickly approached the rear of the Zoox vehicle extending their left arm forward and making contact with the right rear corner of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle operator then disengaged from autonomy and brought the vehicle to a stop. The skateboarder initially told the Zoox vehicle operator they were not injured but later mentioned they “smacked” their hand and it was “bruised.” When asked, however, they declined medical attention. The Zoox vehicle did not sustain damage. The police were not called. The Zoox vehicle camera footage shows that the skateboarder was looking at their cell phone and did not appear to have been looking ahead at the roadway before the time of contact.

A Ghost ADS-equipped car was driving engaged Northbound on Highway 17. As always, there were two safety drivers in the car. Traffic was moving in all four lanes at or near the speed limit. The Ghost vehicle was in the right-middle lane. Another vehicle (the "lead" car) entered into the Ghost car's lane from the right. While there were numerous vehicles ahead of the Ghost car before that vehicle entered the lane, the lead vehicle blocked the view of the lane before it. Throughout the incident, traffic in the other three lanes continued at a steady pace. When the lead vehicle entered into the lane ahead of the Ghost car, the Ghost car applied the brakes to accommodate the intrusion and then continued to match the speed of the lead car. The lead car suddenly slammed the brakes. The Ghost car followed suit, reducing its speed from 19 mps (42.5 mph) to 4.7 mps (10.5 mph) within the next three seconds. The Ghost car was able to match the rapid speed reduction of the lead car and avoid contact. The driver following the Ghost car was not able to respond as quickly as the Ghost ADS. When the following driver began to apply the brakes, the car was about five meters behind and was traveling at 6.5 mps. At the point of impact, the Ghost vehicle was traveling at 4.78 mps (10.7 mph), matching the lead car. There were no injuries. The vehicles suffered only cosmetic damage, the drivers exchanged information, and the Ghost safety drivers returned to home base in conventional mode.

The front left fender of the Waymo AV made contact with the right front panel of the passenger vehicle. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained moderate damage.

narrative: A Zoox vehicle in manual mode came to a stop behind a passenger vehicle that was attempting to parallel park on Montgomery Street. On January 3, 2021 at 9:00 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a heavy truck at the northbound merge lane on the 100 block of Bayshore Boulevard. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). While attempting a merge onto northbound Bayshore Boulevard from southbound Bayshore Boulevard, the Waymo AV came to a stop to yield for approaching traffic on the right. The Waymo AV was rear ended by the truck, causing minor damage to the right rear bumper of the Waymo AV. The truck sustained damage to the left front bumper.

narrative: On January 1, 2021 at 2:04 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Marin Street and Kansas Street. The driver of the Waymo AV transitioned the system into manual mode and slowed, and moved to the right most edge of the lane. The oncoming passenger vehicle struck the left side of the Waymo AV and immediately proceeded to leave the scene of the collision. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained moderate damage to the left front panel and both doors on the left side of the vehicle.

narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was traveling eastbound on Fulton Street in the leftmost lane between 14th Avenue and Park Presidio Boulevard. The Cruise AV braked prior to the Cruise AV operator disengaging the Cruise AV from autonomous mode. The Cruise AV operator continued to brake but, shortly thereafter, the Toyota Sienna made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the front left fender of the Cruise AV. Police were not called to the scene and no injuries were reported.

On December 22, 2021 at 12:35 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Cesar Chavez and Valencia Street. While traveling in manual mode at approximately 25 MPH on westbound Cesar Chavez, the Waymo AV proceeded through a green light into the intersection at Valencia Street. A passenger vehicle traveling southbound on Valencia Street with no headlights on entered the same intersection against the light, making contact with the Waymo AV at approximately 14 MPH. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained moderate damage to the passenger side rear quarter panel. The other vehicle left the scene without exchanging information.

On December 19, 2021 at 10:30 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Fulton Street and 5th Avenue. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV was stopped facing southwest on Fulton Street while yielding to pedestrians in a crosswalk when a passenger vehicle reversed at a low speed from an adjacent driveway into the right rear bumper of the Waymo AV. Both vehicles sustained minor damage.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on northbound Larkin Street at the intersection with Turk Street. The Cruise AV entered the intersection on a green light and continued straight when a cyclist traveling eastbound on Turk Street entered the crosswalk. The Cruise AV braked to the cyclist and, shortly thereafter, another vehicle traveling behind the Cruise AV made contact with the Cruise AV's rear bumper, damaging the rear left bumper. The driver of the other vehicle left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and police were not called.

On December 11, 2021 at 2:28 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco was in a collision involving a concrete post in the parking lot at 1900 Noriega Street. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The operator of the vehicle was attempting to reverse into a parking spot when the right rear sensor casing of the vehicle struck a concrete post adjacent to the parking spot. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to the right rear sensor housing.

A Zoox vehicle was stopped in manual mode while exiting the intersection of Montgomery St. and Pacific St. as a large truck entered the intersection. While the truck began to make a left turn behind the Zoox vehicle, it made contact with the Zoox rear radar and camera pod on the driver's side. There were no injuries and the police were not called.

narrative: On December 7, 2021 at 10:47 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving an SUV at Oak Street at Stanyan Street. While in autonomous mode, the Waymo AV came to a stop at a stop sign on Oak Street. While the ADV was stopped, waiting for a pedestrian to cross and for traffic on Stanyan Street to clear, an SUV approached the Waymo AV from behind and made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to the rear bumper.

The driver of the test vehicle braked but was unable to stop before making contact with the front driver’s side of the Lexus. No injuries were reported and law enforcement was not called to the scene.

On December 4, 2021 at 4:10 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving an SUV on Winson Drive between 19th and 20th Avenues. While in autonomous mode, the Waymo AV turned right from southbound 19th Avenue onto westbound Winston Drive. As the Waymo AV proceeded onto Winston Drive in the far right lane, an SUV also proceeding westbound on Winston Drive made a continuous right lane change from the far left lane, through the middle lane, and entered the far right lane in front of the Waymo AV. The Waymo AV was decelerating when the test driver transitioned to manual mode. The Waymo AV then made contact with the SUV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver (in the driver’s seating position) was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage to its front driver side fender and the SUV sustained damage to its front passenger side fender.

location: 16th Street at Market and Noe Street
narrative: On December 3, 2021 at 12:23 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at 16th Street at Market and Noe Street. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection of 16th Street and Market Street, it stopped behind traffic at a red light. After the Waymo AV was fully stopped, a passenger vehicle reversed out of a parking spot perpendicular to the Waymo AV and made contact with the passenger side rear corner of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present in the driver’s seating position. Both vehicles sustained minor damage to their rear bumpers.

av_damage_areas: left front corner; front bumper; right front corner
narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in manual mode, was traveling eastbound on Hayes Street between Scott Street and Divisadero Street. As the Cruise AV approached the intersection with Divisadero Street, the Cruise AV made contact with the rear bumper of a 2017 Toyota Prius that was stopped at the intersection. This caused damage to the front bumper of the Cruise AV and the rear bumper of the 2017 Toyota Prius. No injuries were reported at the scene by either party. A Cruise AV test driver later sought medical evaluation.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on southbound Laguna Street at the intersection with McAllister Street. Another vehicle approaching from the rear made contact with the Cruise AV's rear bumper, damaging the rear right bumper. The driver of the other vehicle left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and police were not called.

On November 30, 2021 at 12:21pm PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving an SUV on the 10 block of Castro Street. As the Waymo AV test driver drove the Waymo AV in manual mode on southbound Castro Street between Waller Street and Lloyd Street, the passenger side mirror of the Waymo AV made contact with a parked SUV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage to its passenger side rearview mirror.

On November 28, 2021 at 6:08 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Clay Street at Franklin Street. The Waymo AV was stopped at a red light on eastbound Clay Street at Franklin Street when a passenger vehicle struck the Waymo AV’s rear bumper. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV’s rear bumper sustained damage, and the passenger vehicle’s front bumper sustained damage.

location: Scotia Ave, Thornton Ave, and Bridgeview Dr
narrative: On November 26, 2021 at 8:02 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Scotia Avenue, Thornton Avenue, and Bridgeview Drive. The Waymo AV was traveling southbound on Scotia Avenue, a narrow road with vehicles parked on both sides, and approaching the intersection with Thornton Avenue and Bridgeview Drive. A passenger vehicle approaching from the right of the Waymo AV on eastbound Thornton Avenue made a left turn in front of the Waymo AV to head northbound on Scotia Avenue. The Waymo AV slowed to a near stop and nudged to its right in order to share the narrow road with the oncoming vehicle and then came to a stop at the stop sign as the oncoming vehicle completed its turn. At approximately 5 mph, the turning passenger vehicle made contact with Waymo AV’s sensor hardware housing on the driver side rear corner fender of the stopped Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to the sensor hardware housing (which was the reason for towing the Waymo AV) and the passenger vehicle left the scene without exchanging information.

On November 25, 2021 at 1:31 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA made contact with a curb at 32nd Avenue and Taraval Street. While in manual mode, the Waymo AV test driver was completing a right turn from northbound 32nd Avenue onto eastbound Taraval Street when the Waymo AV’s passenger side rear tire made contact with the curb at the corner of the intersection. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV’s passenger side rear tire and wheel sustained minor damage.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on southbound Cayuga Street at the intersection with Geneva Street. As the Cruise AV entered the intersection on a green light and continued southbound on Cayuga Street, a Honda Civic traveling northbound on Cayuga Street initiated an unprotected left turn in the intersection. The Cruise AV hard braked but, shortly thereafter, the Honda Civic made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the back left bumper of the Cruise AV. Police were not called to the scene and no injuries were reported.

On November 20, 2021 at 11:11 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving an SUV on the 1700 block of Steiner Street. The Waymo AV was in autonomous mode and traveling northbound on Steiner Street as it crossed the intersection at Post Street. An SUV then turned right from Post Street onto Steiner Street and began closely following the Waymo AV. The Waymo AV test driver then took manual control and stopped the Waymo AV. The SUV then stopped, reversed, and drove around the Waymo AV and made contact with the Waymo AV’s driver side rear fender. At the time of the impact the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage and the SUV left the scene without exchanging information.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a stop sign on westbound 17th Street at the intersection with Roosevelt Way. Another vehicle approaching from the rear made contact with the Cruise AV's rear bumper. There were no injuries and police were not called. The Cruise AV test operator later mentioned neck pain.

At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV’s rear bumper and undercarriage sustained moderate damage, and the passenger vehicle’s front bumper and hood sustained moderate damage.

Another vehicle approaching from the rear made contact with the Cruise AV's rear bumper, damaging the rear bumper. The driver of the other vehicle left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and police were not called.

narrative: A Cruise autonomous vehicle (Cruise AV), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was traveling westbound on Ocean Avenue between Lee Avenue and Harold Avenue. As the Cruise AV entered the intersection, a 2014 Audi made a prohibited left turn from the rightmost westbound lane on Ocean Ave. The Cruise AV hard braked prior to the Cruise AV operator disengaging the Cruise AV from autonomous mode. The Cruise AV operator continued to hard brake while steering away from the approaching vehicle but, shortly thereafter, the 2014 Audi made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the front right of the Cruise AV and the front left bumper of the 2014 Audi. The Cruise AV was traveling 11.4 mph at the time of contact. Police were not called to the scene and no injuries were reported.

location: Divisadero Street and Golden Gate Avenue
narrative: On November 12, 2021 at 1:23 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Divisadero Street at Turk Street. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage, and the trailing passenger vehicle sustained minor damage.

location: North Fair Oaks Ave and Kifer Road
narrative: A test vehicle, stopped at a red light in Sunnyvale while operating in manual mode, was lightly struck on a sensor attached to the rear driver side wheel by a white minivan attempting to maneuver around the vehicle to enter a left turn lane. The test vehicle’s sensor was not damaged. The minivan left the scene without stopping, so any damage to the minivan is unknown. No injuries were reported, and law enforcement was not called to the scene.

On November 6, 2021 at 1:50 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Waller Street at Alpine Terrace. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound on Waller Street when it yielded to an oncoming passenger vehicle. As the passenger vehicle passed the stopped Waymo AV, its driver side rearview mirror made contact with a Waymo AV sensor. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained minor damage.

On November 6, 2021 at 4:28 PM PDT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Powell Street at Pacific Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling in autonomous mode southbound on Powell Street when it activated its right turn signal and prepared to make a right turn onto Pacific Avenue. The Waymo AV stopped to yield to a pedestrian who was in the adjacent crosswalk on Pacific Avenue. A passenger vehicle behind the Waymo AV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to its rear bumper, and the trailing passenger vehicle sustained minor damage to its front bumper.

narrative: On November 4, 2021 at 6:41 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA made contact with a fixed object at the intersection of Icehouse Alley and Green Street. The Waymo AV was traveling eastbound on Green Street when the vehicle approached a partially covered manhole. The manhole cover made contact with the underside of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to the underside of the car.

At 3:27 PM on 11/03/2021, a driver from Weride was operating one of our autonomous vehicles in autonomous mode on the on-ramp to CA 87 S from Charcot Avenue in North San Jose. Our car was in the queue of traffic waiting for the metering light. While our car was stationary (0 MPH), the other car involved accelerated slightly to about 5 MPH, which resulted in a minor rear end collision. Our driver and the other party pulled over onto the shoulder. There were no injuries and information was exchanged. Since damage to our car was minimal, it was driven back to the office in manual mode.

location: Intersection of Oakdell and Lemon St.
narrative: A Zoox vehicle was in manual mode making a left turn from Lemon St. onto Oakdell St.. A passenger vehicle passed through a stop sign without slowing and made contact with the rear and left side of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle incurred minor damage to its rear, left bumper and rear sensor. There were no injuries and the police were not called.

While performing the lane change, the Pony.ai AV came into contact with a center divider on Fremont Blvd. and the traffic sign that was posted on the divider. The Pony.ai AV suffered moderate damage to the front of the vehicle and the undercarriage. There were no injuries and no other vehicles involved. Fremont Police Department were called to report the incident and the damaged street sign. Pony.ai has subsequently worked with local authorities to resolve all issues related to the damaged sign.

On October 28, 2021 at 9:35 PM PDT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, CA was in a collision involving a van at Silver Avenue at Bayshore Boulevard. The Waymo AV, while in autonomous mode, was waiting to make a left turn from Silver Avenue onto Bayshore Boulevard and yielding to oncoming traffic, when the test driver (in the driver’s seating position) transitioned to manual mode and proceeded with a left turn manually. During the left turn, an approaching van made contact with the front bumper of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage to its front bumper, and the van sustained minor damage to its front bumper.

On October 27, 2021 at 3:54 PM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle at Flower Street and Bayshore Avenue. While in manual mode, the operator of the Waymo AV was at a complete stop while yielding to traffic approaching from the left, waiting to make a left turn onto Bayshore Avenue from northwest Flower Street. A passenger vehicle approached from behind and made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained minor damage.
